camera.position: the view is Nora's own eyes as she rides astride the juvenile Triceratops just behind its frill, facing forward in the direction it gallops; all recording gear is completely outside the visible frame
camera.framing: the back of the Triceratops's frill rim and the tips of its two brow horns fill the bottom of the frame; Nora's two hands, in long golden-tan suede sleeves, grip the frill rim at the bottom left and bottom right; the muddy path runs ahead through the centre

setting.location: Hell Creek floodplain forest, Montana, Late Cretaceous, 66 million years ago, warm humid late morning
elements: a humid riverside forest of broadleaf flowering trees and shrubs mixed with tall straight dawn redwood trunks; hazy sunlight slants in from the upper left; low ferns and leafy shrubs line a soft wet mud path with puddles; no grass anywhere; warm and humid, no snow, no frost

two massive dawn redwood trunks stand close together on both sides of the path about twenty-five meters ahead from frame 0; the path itself passes between them, in the same plane as the running Triceratops; the gap is only just wider than the Triceratops; they stay in that spot for the whole clip
the only animal in the frame is the Triceratops Nora rides; no other animals, no birds in the frame, no people

characters.name: Nora
characters.visual_lock: matches the Nora face and Nora Body reference images (her own hands and sleeves); her face is never shown because the view is her own eyes; only her two hands and sleeves are visible
characters.outfit: her sleeves are the long golden-tan suede tunic sleeves of the Nora Body reference, reaching all the way to her wrists
characters.action: rides astride the Triceratops; for the whole clip both hands grip the frill rim at the bottom left and bottom right of the frame, knuckles tight, and never let go, even while she talks; she speaks off-screen, breathless

characters.name: Juvenile Triceratops
characters.visual_lock: matches the Juvenile Triceratops reference image exactly: pony-sized, olive-brown pebbly hide with darker mottled bands, short brow horns curving backward, a short rounded frill edged with small triangular bumps
characters.position: carries Nora and gallops straight ahead along the path and through the gap between the two trunks; it never turns

timeline_action.0-3s: From frame 0 the Triceratops is already galloping straight along the path and the two close trunks stand ahead in the centre of the frame, small in the distance. By 3 seconds they fill the middle third of the frame. Nora speaks from second 0, off-screen.
timeline_action.3-7s: The trunks grow until they fill the frame on both sides. At about 5 seconds the Triceratops passes through the gap: the left trunk sweeps past the left edge of the frame and the right trunk past the right edge, close enough to see the bark texture blur; the frill rim passes between them without touching.
timeline_action.7-10s: Beyond the trunks the path opens ahead and the Triceratops keeps galloping straight. Nora finishes her line by about 9 seconds; the last half second is only the bouncing gallop.

0-3s.Juvenile Triceratops: straight gallop toward the gap, mud flying

7-10s.Juvenile Triceratops: keeps galloping straight along the open path

motion_choreography.end_state: The two trunks are behind them and out of the frame; the open path runs ahead; both hands still grip the frill rim.

speech.speaker: Nora
speech.voice_profile: Laomedeia, breathless and panicked, rising into a cracking shout in danger, then a relieved laugh

segments.3-7s: Squeeze through, squeeze through, keep your head down!
segments.7-10s: We made it through! It's way too big to follow!

delivery.7-10s: Nora shouts (breaking into a relieved laugh)

speech.dialogue: There, between those two trees, go straight! Squeeze through, squeeze through, keep your head down! We made it through! It's way too big to follow!

audio.ambience: rushing forest air, low under her voice
audio.sfx: the Triceratops's pounding footfalls and mud splashes, low under her voice; heavy distant footfalls far behind, low under her voice

physical_realism.force_and_traction: each Triceratops footfall slaps into the wet mud and throws clods forward and sideways; its shoulders drive up and down under the rider
physical_realism.secondary_motion: the frill rim and brow horns bob with every stride a beat behind the shoulders; fern fronds whip past both edges of the frame and spring back
physical_realism.environment: hazy sunbeams between the trees, flying mud droplets catching the light, puddles splashing; the bark of the two trunks rushes past both edges of the frame at about 5 seconds
physical_realism.camera_response: a hard vertical bounce on every Triceratops stride and a slight side-to-side sway with its shoulders; the view never floats smoothly and never turns to look backward
physical_realism.documentary_texture: matte, dry, weathered scaly hides caked with real mud, real contact shadows under the animals, natural available light only, slight motion blur on fast legs; looks like real handheld wildlife footage of living animals, not CGI, not a game, not toys, not animatronics

the view stays on the Triceratops's back until the last frame and her two hands stay visible on the frill rim until the last frame; the Triceratops never walks away from the view
